why_this_matters: Day 153 sits in Phase 9 (Excel + Power BI + Tableau), whose goal is: Be dangerous in the BI stack that most employers actually use. Today's core material - TEXT, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, TRIM, CONCAT/TEXTJOIN, Date functions and date arithmetic, PivotTable fields, values, filters - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: Display each of the 16 original digits together with its compressed binary representation, and the reconstructed digit.
code.code:
#@title

def display_digits(originals, strings, entropies, reconstructions):
  """Visualizes 16 digits together with their reconstructions."""
  fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 4, sharex=True, sharey=True, figsize=(12.5, 5))
  axes = axes.ravel()
  for i in range(len(axes)):
    image = tf.concat([
        tf.squeeze(originals[i]),
        tf.zeros((28, 14), tf.uint8),
        tf.squeeze(reconstructions[i]),
    ], 1)
    axes[i].imshow(image)
    axes[i].text(
        .5, .5, f"→ 0x{strings[i].numpy().hex()} →\n{entropies[i]:0.2f} bits",
        ha="center", va="top", color="white", fontsize="small",
        transform=axes[i].transAxes)
    axes[i].axis("off")
  plt.subplots_adjust(wspace=0, hspace=0, left=0, right=1, bottom=0, top=1)

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using TEXT, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, TRIM, CONCAT/TEXTJOIN on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
